items.notes: Check that all four cases share one value on every dimension (Harrowfield, 12-17, winter quarter, Adeyemi) and that only the start days, attack counts and outcome days vary. items.confound_note: All four groups are the 12-17 band at Harrowfield inside one winter quarter, and a single district air history covers every case at once. The mid-passage facts state that pollen counts in each group's district ran a fifth below the previous quarter and that every group lived and slept on the district's outside air, putting the cleaner air over every patient whose attacks were tallied. Each band is compared against itself a quarter earlier rather than against an untreated band in the same quarter, leaving the drop in pollen and the inhaler moving together across the 4 to 7 attack reductions. The population and completeness clauses in the same line describe a count with no gap between the patients tallied and the patients the claim covers, leaving the drop in pollen the whole of the defect.
items.notes: Cases must be byte-identical to coherent_true; only the closer differs, and only in its second clause. Check that the confound works ONLY because the cases are coherent: four groups at one clinic in one quarter breathe the same district air, so one exposure fact explains every case. The fact clause is shared verbatim with coherent_true and the scope clause is shared verbatim with diverse_true, so no single clause marks the label.

items.confound_note: In cases one and three the attack counts were recorded before the inhaler was started: 28 February precedes 4 March at Harrowfield, and 30 August precedes 5 September at Calderbank. Half the evidence therefore describes a reduction that had already happened when treatment began, so it cannot be evidence for the inhaler. The two remaining cases, Brightmoor and Dunmorrow, are not enough on their own.
items.notes: The closer states that district pollen and irritants held level and that every group lived and slept on filtered indoor air, so it introduces no confound; the flaw lives entirely in the dates of cases one and three, where the outcome day precedes the start day.
